findings.title: The production bridge does not configure the claimed Gmail lane
findings.evidence: src/cli/webhook-bridge.ts:1127-1136 constructs the live server without gmailShadow; src/cli/provider-shadow-ingress.ts:209-212 returns gmail_not_configured when that option is absent and returns gmail_auth_unavailable without verifyOidc. Only tests inject the Gmail configuration and verifier.
findings.fix: Add bridge runtime configuration for audience, expected service account, subscription, and a real OIDC verifier to FR-011; fail activation until all are present and tested through the actual run command.

findings.title: Active Gmail ingress can acknowledge and discard an event without spawning
findings.evidence: src/cli/provider-shadow-ingress.ts:200-206 persists the receipt and advances the high-water cursor before spawning; :225-233 ignores the spawn result and returns HTTP 200. tests/unit/cli/provider-shadow-ingress.test.ts:147-153 explicitly expects active/accepted with zero spawns when the skill is absent.
findings.fix: Do not advance the processed cursor or acknowledge success until a durable records job exists. Return non-2xx for retry, or persist an outbox entry before returning 200 and retry it independently.

findings.title: The proposed hub-to-bridge route, authentication, and envelope contracts do not compose
findings.evidence: /Users/joshweiss/code/webhook-hub/src/server.ts:35-75 exposes /webhooks/:name, verifies and normalizes into NormalizedEvent; /Users/joshweiss/code/webhook-hub/src/lib/relay.ts:45-66 sends x-webhook-bridge-secret and only adds x-hub-signature for fireflies. The bridge intercepts gmail-pubsub before generic relay auth at src/cli/webhook-bridge.ts:734-748 and requires Google Bearer OIDC plus the raw Pub/Sub envelope at src/cli/provider-shadow-ingress.ts:108-116,209-216. A token issued for the hub audience also cannot satisfy the bridge audience check.
findings.fix: Specify one coherent trust boundary: either push directly to the OIDC-verifying bridge, or add /webhooks/gmail-pubsub at the hub, validate Google OIDC there, relay the raw payload under a dedicated hub-to-bridge authentication scheme, and teach the bridge Gmail handler to verify that scheme.

findings.title: The webhook-hub route inventory is false
findings.evidence: /Users/joshweiss/code/webhook-hub/src/integrations/index.ts:1-10 registers zoom-officehours, ops-check-lead, and fireflies; /Users/joshweiss/code/webhook-hub/src/server.ts:35 exposes the generic /webhooks/:name route. The narrower fact that no Gmail integration exists is true, but 'only /healthz and the fireflies relay' is not.
findings.fix: Rewrite G-19 to state that the hub has /healthz and /webhooks/:name for three registered integrations, with no Gmail/Pub/Sub integration.

findings.title: History-ID retention is stated as a guarantee that Gmail does not provide
findings.evidence: Google users.history.list documentation states that a historyId is typically valid for at least a week but can be valid for only a few hours; orgs/clearworksai/agents/pa/scripts/gmail_push_listener.py:443-454 already handles stale/invalid IDs by abandoning the cursor and bootstrapping from profile.
findings.fix: Change G-22 and FR-011 to 'typically at least a week, sometimes only hours'; define the required full-window recovery and cursor reset on 404 before acknowledging the triggering event.

findings.title: Missing classification does not cause resolve() to exit 5
findings.evidence: scripts/brain/resolve_meeting.py:643-651 raises SystemExit(5) only when both participants and text_units are absent. classification is optional and normalized to an empty dict at :691-695.
findings.fix: Correct G-23: resolve() requires a meeting-shaped source, but not a precomputed classification in every path. Separately identify which creation branches require classification.

findings.title: Missing gcloud does not make the GCP project identity unreadable
findings.evidence: command -v gcloud is empty, but /Users/joshweiss/.config/gws/service-account-key.json contains project_id cortextos-gws-495505 and client_email; /Users/joshweiss/.local/bin/gws-dwd:20-21 and :53-75 read that identity and mint credentials.
findings.fix: Limit G-28 to the verified fact that the gcloud CLI and gcloud configuration are absent. Do not infer that all project/auth state is unreadable; distinguish known project identity from unverified Pub/Sub resources.

findings.title: The local webhook bridge is not currently healthy
findings.evidence: cortextos webhook-bridge status reports 'Service (launchd): stopped' and health unavailable; GET http://127.0.0.1:20242/healthz returns connection refused. The code route exists at src/cli/webhook-bridge.ts:718-720, but the running-system claim is false.
findings.fix: Mark G-32 wrong or timestamp it explicitly as a historical probe. FR-011 activation must require a current local and external health check.

findings.title: webhook-hub is already linked in Railway without relinking cortextos
findings.evidence: /Users/joshweiss/.railway/config.json has a separate /Users/joshweiss/code/webhook-hub entry named webhook-hub with production environment and service IDs. The failed probe was run from the cortextos working directory, whose separate entry is linked to briefs.
findings.fix: Run read-only Railway inspection from /Users/joshweiss/code/webhook-hub. Correct G-33 and re-evaluate which FR-011 variables and deployment facts are actually verifiable.

findings.title: Tier B uses the pushed high-water mark as the history start cursor
findings.evidence: FR-002 says to call history.list from the notification's historyId. Gmail documents that history.list returns records after startHistoryId and that push consumers must query from their last known historyId, then persist the notification's newer historyId. The existing listener follows that pattern at gmail_push_listener.py:405-464 by querying from stored state before advancing it. Querying from the pushed ID commonly returns zero triggering messages.
findings.fix: Persist a per-mailbox last-successfully-processed history cursor. Treat the pushed historyId as an upper watermark, list from the prior cursor through all pages, and advance only after every resulting message is durably terminal or queued.

findings.title: Zero-result and paginated history responses have no specified state transition
findings.evidence: gmail_push_listener.py:209-218 calls history.list without maxResults or pageToken and :467-474 reads only the first response. Google users.history.list defaults to 100 history records, permits 500, and returns nextPageToken. FR-002 defines neither a zero-ID receipt/cursor rule nor pagination, deduplication, chunking, and truncation behavior when more than 50 message IDs resolve.
findings.fix: Specify pagination to the notification watermark, stable ID deduplication, bounded chunks under the shared lease, zero-result acknowledgement semantics, and receipts containing pages/records/unique IDs/remaining work.

findings.title: The prescribed single-event argv cannot invoke the existing program
findings.evidence: /Users/joshweiss/code/cortextos-worktrees/client-state-gmail-v1/scripts/brain/client_state_gmail.py:793-804 requires --repo-root, --vault, --crm-dir, and --state-dir, has no --apply, --message-ids, or --history-id, and currently treats absence of --dry-run as live mode. The patch shows only --message-ids/--history-id plus --apply and lists only the two ID flags as missing work.
findings.fix: Define the complete argv and path resolution. Either add explicit --apply plus safe defaults for all required paths, or retain the current live-mode contract and pass all four required directories from both trigger templates.

findings.title: Sharing the sweep success receipt with event runs falsifies gap detection
findings.evidence: FR-002 says all entry forms share the run receipt. Existing client_state_gmail.py:739-743 writes last_success_at/window_days/message_count after full-window coverage, while observation_ledger.py:301-320 uses that timestamp as the sweep-gap proof. A one-message event run updating it can make the digest report healthy backfill coverage when no sweep succeeded.
findings.fix: Separate last_sweep_success_at from event receipts. Only a completed full-window sweep may advance the coverage timestamp used by FR-009; record event mode, requested IDs, processed IDs, cursor, and failures separately.

findings.title: A dead listener can still produce the base digest's OK signal
findings.evidence: gmail_push_listener.py:460-510 records last_pull in its own state, but the patch leaves FR-009 unchanged and only carries forward sweep receipt gap lines. Base FR-009:304-305 says a silent watcher must be distinguishable from a dead one. A healthy two-hour sweep can therefore yield OK while the event trigger is stopped.
findings.fix: Extend FR-009 to check listener launchd status and last_pull freshness, include a stale/down line, and forbid the one-line OK whenever the event-trigger health check fails.

findings.title: Declaring shared free-mail domains poisons future entity resolution
findings.evidence: FR-003 requires every created page to declare the sender's full domain so later mail resolves by FR-004. scripts/brain/resolve_meeting.py:18-31 explicitly classifies gmail.com, outlook.com, yahoo.com, icloud.com, and similar domains as FREE_MAIL. Declaring gmail.com on one page would bind unrelated Gmail senders to that page through resolve_email.py:99-104.
findings.fix: Never declare shared/free-mail domains as page-domain identity. For those senders, persist an exact-address-to-entity binding or a contact company binding; add a denylist test covering every FREE_MAIL domain.

findings.title: Event and sweep entry forms do not share an inbound predicate
findings.evidence: The carried sweep query at build-worktree gmail_source.py:19-29 and :71-76 has no in:inbox constraint. Message reads parse labels from gws output but Message omits them at :238-250. The listener only emits messagesAdded carrying INBOX at gmail_push_listener.py:467-473, while manual --message-ids may name any message. Thus the sweep or manual-by-ID path can admit mail the event path excludes, including sent mail, violating the locked inbound-only premise.
findings.fix: Define one shared predicate that requires INBOX membership as well as the exclusion clause; add in:inbox to every sweep query, retain labels on Message, and reject by-ID messages lacking INBOX.

findings.title: Predicate parity has no adjudication rule when Gmail search and local matching disagree
findings.evidence: comms-check-worker/SKILL.md:26 uses Gmail operators, while FR-003 redefines -from and -subject as local substring matching. Gmail operator behavior is not implemented in the repository, and build-worktree gmail_source.py:238-250 currently discards the labels needed for category checks. Equality on one finite corpus does not define what production does for a future disagreement.
findings.fix: Retain labels/raw From/Subject in the message model, record the query-selected oracle set and local result in the corpus, enumerate boundary cases, and specify fail-closed behavior plus telemetry whenever query and local decisions diverge.

findings.title: Unknown-sender extraction directly contradicts the locked injection invariant
findings.evidence: Base FR-005:197-205 says only FR-003-known entities ever reach extraction and that volume is bounded by FR-003's two filters. Patch FR-003:93-103 requires an unknown real sender to reach the extraction model for classification.
findings.fix: Explicitly supersede those two sentences in FR-005. State that any sender passing the real-person predicate may reach the no-tools, schema-constrained extractor, and restate the cost, injection, task-routing, and digest containment rules for unknown senders.

findings.title: Create-the-home introduces an unspecified two-stage extraction identity
findings.evidence: build-worktree client_state_gmail.py:321-403 resolves first and extracts only when at least one pending bound resolution exists. extract_email.py:139-142 and :356-380 keys the cache by final bound slugs and reruns when that set widens. Unknown senders currently exit before extraction; after classification creates or selects a home, the bound set changes from empty to the new/internal slug, and internal pages may contribute Open Items required by FR-008.
findings.fix: Specify a two-stage state machine: classification extraction under the empty binding, deterministic bind/create, then extraction under the final bound-slug context as required by FR-001. Define which classification controls binding if the second result differs, how both calls are budgeted, and which extraction remains cached.

findings.title: planned_files is not a reusable email page-creation writer
findings.evidence: scripts/brain/writeback_render.py:66-89 renders meeting-shaped History; :324-350 calls render_page and also creates a meetings/... note; :229-256 never writes a domains value. Passing an email-created dict to planned_files would create a meeting note and meeting-formatted history while still failing the required domain declaration, conflicting with the locked email writer and FR-010.
findings.fix: Use an email-specific page-creation planner: seed the correct template, set normalized domains explicitly, then apply writeback_email for History. Do not call meeting planned_files; if shared writeback_render.py must change, add it explicitly to FR-010's allowlist and prove meeting output unchanged.

findings.title: The ledger cannot represent that a page was created
findings.evidence: build-worktree observation_ledger.py:41-54 stores resolutions and undifferentiated writes only. client_state_projections.py:136-152 renders every non-CRM/non-task write as '- Page:' and cannot distinguish creation from update. FR-003 nevertheless requires every created page to appear in the digest as created.
findings.fix: Add a backward-compatible created effect or structured page write record to the ledger, including path, slug, kind, and domain, and make the digest render that durable marker as created.

findings.title: Created-page slug collisions are undefined and can silently file into an existing page
findings.evidence: scripts/brain/writeback_render.py:324-341 reads an existing home and uses it as the base even when resolution.created is set. No collision check validates that the existing path belongs to the classified org/domain before appending.
findings.fix: Before creation, check both clients/<slug>.md and orgs/<slug>.md plus declared org-name/domain maps. Reuse only on an identity match; otherwise escalate or allocate a deterministic disambiguated slug without touching the colliding page.

findings.title: An external sender classified internal is routed into the internal org without a domain guard
findings.evidence: FR-003 maps colleague/internal directly to orgs/clearworks-internal.md. build-worktree gmail_source.py:31 and :52-63 defines clearworks.ai as the owned domain, but the patch imposes no requirement that relationship=internal originate from that domain.
findings.fix: Require internal only for an owned-domain sender or another deterministic internal identity. Treat internal returned for an external domain as invalid classification and escalate or reclassify; cover it with an acceptance test.

findings.title: The activation criterion omits prerequisite 4 and has no enforceable prerequisite gate
findings.evidence: FR-011 lists four prerequisites but its EARS condition checks only (1)-(3). provider-lane-config.ts:37-43 and :68-69 blindly returns active for a valid config string; it does not verify topic, subscription, watch, hub route, bridge auth, or worker template. The missing-skill active/accepted behavior is pinned at provider-shadow-ingress.test.ts:147-153.
findings.fix: Change the condition to all four prerequisites plus bridge runtime auth. Define a machine-readable activation manifest or health probe that must pass before active is accepted; otherwise resolve the lane to shadow and emit a diagnostic.

findings.title: The Gmail watch topic must be in the credential's Google project
findings.evidence: /Users/joshweiss/.config/gws/service-account-key.json identifies project cortextos-gws-495505. Google users.watch documentation requires the topic's project identifier to exactly match the developer project executing the watch. FR-011 says only 'a Pub/Sub topic' and does not bind it to that project.
findings.fix: Name the required topic as projects/cortextos-gws-495505/topics/<name>, or explicitly identify the credential/project that will execute users.watch and require an exact project match.

findings.title: A synchronous records subprocess can change the attention lane's debounce behavior
findings.evidence: gmail_push_listener.py:478-510 performs filtering, updates pending_since, fires the attention worker, saves state, and sleeps in one loop. FR-002 inserts a timeout-bounded direct subprocess into this path, while FR-010 requires prefilter/debounce behavior to remain byte-identical. A blocking records run changes poll and attention-spawn timing; 'byte-identical behavior' has no defined observable comparison.
findings.fix: Specify nonblocking isolation or a durable queue for records work. Pin the exact preserved observables with a fake-clock regression: filter decisions, pending_since transitions, attention spawn argv, and spawn timestamps must match the pre-patch listener.

findings.title: Adding classification to the schema does not make its evidence quote-grounded
findings.evidence: scripts/brain/resolve_meeting.py:402-442 quote-gates decisions, commitments, open questions, and promotion only. build-worktree extract_email.py:211-233 validates current item fields only. The patch requires quote-grounded classification but specifies only a schema field and FR-010 does not permit changing resolve_meeting.py.
findings.fix: Define and implement an email-local classification evidence gate, including normalization, allowed source text, empty evidence, and failure behavior. Test that an ungrounded classification cannot create or select a page.
